issues.legal_issue: A party commits contempt by completing a restrained transfer of property after a court order forbids further allotments, even when an agreement of sale was made before the order.
material_facts: The Court had ordered that no further allotments of flats be made while the proceedings were pending.
The respondent claimed that an agreement of sale for the flats had been entered into before the order; the Court assumed the agreement was genuine without deciding that question.
After the order, the respondent delivered possession of the flats to third parties and registered sale deeds in their favour.
The respondent did not seek clarification of the order before proceeding with delivery of possession and registration.
issues.conclusion: The respondent violated the order and was guilty of contempt. In context, the prohibition on further allotments covered making over the flats, including delivery of possession and registration of sale deeds; it was not confined to entering into agreements of sale.
issues.legal_principle: An order must be interpreted reasonably and in its context. Here, the term “allotment” covered the effective transfer of the flats by delivery of possession and registration of sale deeds; a party could not adopt a restrictive interpretation that rendered the order nugatory, and should have sought clarification if genuinely in doubt. The Court held the respondent guilty of contempt and imposed punishment under Section 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: contempt_proceeding and order_barred_further_transfers and possession_delivered_after_order and sale_deeds_registered_after_order

predicates.contempt_proceeding: The proceeding asked the court to determine whether a party had disobeyed a court order.
predicates.order_barred_further_transfers: The court had ordered a party not to make further transfers of the relevant property.
predicates.possession_delivered_after_order: The party delivered possession of the property to third parties after the order was made.
predicates.sale_deeds_registered_after_order: The party registered sale deeds transferring the property to third parties after the order was made.

issues.definition: When a contempt proceeding concerns an order barring further property transfers, and the party delivers possession and registers sale deeds afterward, the party commits contempt.

issues.legal_issue: A court may reject an apology for contempt when it is qualified by a defence of the conduct or when the contemnor’s conduct shows persistent disregard for the court’s orders.
material_facts: The respondent tendered an apology while asserting that any breach resulted from mistake, inadvertence, or misunderstanding.
In the same affidavit, the respondent repeated the arguments defending the conduct that the Court had rejected.
The Court found that the respondent had persistently flouted its orders and treated the Court’s authority with disregard.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the apology, finding it was not truly unconditional and that the respondent’s conduct would warrant rejection even if it were treated as unconditional.
issues.legal_principle: The Court may decline to accept an apology in contempt proceedings where it is not genuine and unconditional or where the contemnor’s conduct makes acceptance inappropriate. No statutory provision or earlier case was identified as the basis for this part of the ruling.

predicates.contempt_proceeding: The proceeding asked the court to determine and address alleged disobedience of a court order.
predicates.apology_qualified_by_defence: The contemnor tendered an apology while continuing to defend the conduct said to breach the order.
predicates.conduct_showed_persistent_disregard: The contemnor’s conduct showed repeated disregard for the court’s orders.

issues.definition: In a contempt proceeding, the court rejects an apology if it is qualified by a defence or the contemnor’s conduct shows persistent disregard.

issues.legal_issue: A court may impose imprisonment and a fine for contempt having regard to the circumstances and seriousness of the disobedience.
material_facts: The respondent was found guilty of contempt for acting contrary to the Court’s order.
The Court characterized the violation as brazen and found that the respondent had consistently flouted its orders.
The Court rejected the respondent’s apology.
issues.conclusion: The Court imposed imprisonment and a fine on the respondent for contempt.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 provides the basis for punishment for contempt. The Court selected the sentence having regard to the facts and circumstances, including the seriousness of the violation and the respondent’s conduct. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.contempt_proceeding: The proceeding asked the court to determine and address alleged disobedience of a court order.
predicates.contempt_found: The court found that the respondent had committed contempt.
predicates.serious_disobedience: The respondent’s breach was brazen and formed part of conduct showing persistent flouting of court orders.

issues.definition: In a contempt proceeding, when the court finds contempt involving serious disobedience, it may impose imprisonment and a fine.
